title: Special Topics in Critical Thinkers
description: Explores in depth the work of one particular thinker relevant to the field of media and cultural studies, for example, Freud, Barthes, Benjamin, and others.

title: Rhetoric of Film Theories
description: Examines the forms of language and conventions of reasoning that sustain major film theories.

title: Narrative Theory and Memory
description: Theories of narrative and their relationship to the human mind, traumatic experience, and the evocation of emotion.

title: Feminism and Media Theory
description: An intellectual history of feminist film and television theory from the 1970s to the present. Course readings are discussed in relation to gender representations in various screenings. Areas covered include psychoanalysis, structuralism, poststructuralism, queer theory, and cultural studies.

title: Digital Media Theory and Practices
description: Studies the emerging theoretical paradigms and creative practices of new media technologies including the Internet, computer games, CD-ROM, DVD, and wireless communication devices. Also examines how technologies mediate, perpetuate, and challenge social, cultural, political, and economic institutions and humanistic values.

title: Postcolonial Media Theory
description: Studies colonial ideologies and representations, and postcolonial challenges and negotiations, with an emphasis on concepts such as imperialism, Eurocentricism, Orientalism, Third Cinema, hybridity, voice, and identity. Interrogates the institutions, frameworks, and processes involved in the production of knowledge.

title: Cultural Theory
description: Explores key ideas, issues, and developments in cultural studies and critical theory through close readings of primary texts. Possible approaches include the Frankfurt School, the Birmingham School, Freudianism/Lacanianism, semiotics/structuralism, and postmodernism/post-structuralism.

title: Popular Culture
description: Surveys contemporary approaches to the study of popular culture. Readings include theorists who have critically engaged the Frankfurt School, who have written before and beyond the Birmingham School, or who have taken a comparative international perspective.

title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies
description: Close examination of a topic in cultural studies.

title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Alchemy and Reverie
description: Explores media and the idea of mediation in relation to mystical, esoteric, and occult symbols and traditions. How can alchemy (the ancient art of transmutation) and reverie (the psychology of daydreaming) inspire us to reimagine present-day technologies and popular cultures?

title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Animal, Vegetable, Mineral
description: Explores nascent trends in environmental media studiese.g. elemental media, blue humanities, cold humanities, thermocultures, geology of mediaand their intersections with ongoing debates in animal studies, plant philosophy, game studies, critical infrastructure studies, and science and technology studies.

title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Media and Datification
description: In this seminar, we explore how processes of datification and machine learning and AI tools are being used to reconfigure media technologies, industries, content, and audiences. Topics to be discussed include: recommendation systems and taste, "blackboxing" and the politics of transparency/opacity, algorithmic bias and racism, the labor of content moderation, data storage and distribution, and online tracking and surveillance, among other issues.

title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Media Risk
description: This seminar interrogates mediations of risk, uncertainty, and speculation, to theorize the concept of "risk media." Among its primary concerns are 1) risk as the taming of uncertainty, 2) risk, as coming harm, requiring mediation to become legible, and 3) radical uncertainty inspiring speculative media.

title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Occult Correspondences
description: This course puts media, cultural, and literary theory into correspondence with esoteric, occult, and alchemical symbols and traditions. Topics include: magic and mimesis, crystal poetics, anomalous phenomena, reverie and imagination, hermeneutics of the symbol, divinatory technologies, and postcolonial astrology.

title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Oil Modernity
description: This seminar examines how our dependency on oil shapes modern ways of seeing and being. It draws together current literature and debates in humanistic scholarship on energy justice with an emphasis on perspectives from the Global South and Indigenous North.

title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Political Media
description: Explores the changing nature of film, TV, radio, the internet, blogs, and social/interactive media in the political firmament of U.S. Taking into account powerful influences from YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, Instagram and other social media outlets, the course considers whether such new media technologies and their rapid diffusion among diverse population blocs represent a paradigm shift in how contemporary politics function. Organizations such as MoveOn.org, Obama for America, American Crossroads, and additionally, the consequences of net neutrality regulations, the 'Viral Civil Rights Movement,' the Arab Spring uprising, local and global online political economies, 'Citizens United,' and more will come under scrutiny.

title: Race, Immigration, and White Supremacy in California
description: California was part of the Spanish empire before it was incorporated into the United States under the Treaty of Guadalupe with Mexico. This interdisciplinary course explores the legacies of colonialism and the logics of white supremacy as they continue to shape the migration experience to California. This course considers internal migration from other regions of the United States, and migration from Asia. One goal of this course is to challenge and rethink the mythologies of migration and the California Dream, while excavating the varied experiences of privileged and precarious migration.

title: Sound and Aurality
description: Explores the interdisciplinary field of sound studies from a variety of critical historiographical and theoretical perspectives. Topics include architectural acoustics, eco-sonic media, vibrational ontologies, sound-reproduction technologies, noise and feedback, sonic warfare, aurality and modern rationality.

title: Psychoanalysis and Cultural Studies
description: Even though Freud was an early modern theorist of popular culture and everyday life, the emergent field of cultural studies has paid little attention to the insights of psychoanalysis. What could cultural studies learn from psychoanalysis and vice versa?

title: The Inhuman and Posthuman in Digital Culture
description: Examines the rhetorics and aesthetics of digital media technologies, especially as they construct new epistemologies and ontologies of representing/mediating the human condition, paying particular attention to claims that new digital technologies have transformed the liberal Enlightenment subject into the posthuman.

title: Gaming Culture
description: The computer games industry rivals film and television for audience discretionary income. This course focuses on computer game theories, genres, aesthetics, industrial histories and practices, and representational discourses.

title: Film and Ethnography
description: Brings the techniques of film analysis to bear on the films, videos, and writings of leading visual anthropologists, such as Tim Asch, Jorge Preloran, and Dennis O'Rourke.

title: Special Topics in Film and/or Media Globalization
description: Close examination of a topic in globalization of film and/or media.
